## 1. Normality Check of Variables

### i. Raw Variables

Now continuous variables must be checked for Normality by Shapiro-Wilk's method.

Identify which columns contain the variables of interest

```{r}
library(dplyr)

# Create a string of variable names that are numeric
numeric_vars <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(where(is.numeric)) %>%
  names()

# Call out variable names
numeric_vars
```

Normality and skewness checks of numeric variables

```{r}

#load package (must be installed first)
library(fBasics)

# Initialize results data frame
normality_results <- data.frame(
  Variable = numeric_vars,
  Normality = NA_character_,
  Skewness = NA_real_,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Loop over columns
for (i in seq_along(numeric_vars)) {
  var_data <- dat[[numeric_vars[i]]]
  
  # Ensure numeric
  if (!is.numeric(var_data)) {
    normality_results$Normality[i] <- "Not numeric"
    normality_results$Skewness[i] <- NA
    next
  }
  
  # Run Shapiro-Wilk normality test
  test_result <- tryCatch({
    normalTest(var_data, method = "sw")
  }, error = function(e) NULL)
  
  if (!is.null(test_result)) {
    # Normality Pass/Fail
    normality_results$Normality[i] <- ifelse(test_result@test$p.value > 0.05, "Pass", "Fail")
  } else {
    normality_results$Normality[i] <- "Error"
  }
  
  # Calculate skewness
  normality_results$Skewness[i] <- skewness(var_data)
}

# View results
print(normality_results)
```

Save to excel

```{r}
library(openxlsx)

# Create a new workbook for flowing tributary sites
wb <- createWorkbook("EDA_HA10%_Closed_System.xlsx")

# Create sheet if it does NOT exist
if(!"Normality checks" %in% names(wb)) {
  addWorksheet(wb, "Normality checks")
}

# Write your new table
writeData(wb, "Normality checks", normality_results)

# Save the workbook (overwrite)
saveWorkbook(wb, "EDA_HA10%_Closed_System.xlsx", overwrite = TRUE)
```

All but 2 variables were not Normally distributed and, generally, variables were left-skewed (positive)

### ii. Log-Transformed Variables

Now we'll perform the same functions on the log-transformed variables (except pH since it's already log-transformed). We'll add a +1 constant to variables since log-transformations cannot be performed on 0 values.

```{r}
library(dplyr)

# Exclude the following variables from being log-transformed
exclude_vars <- c(
  "pH",
  "Relative_elevation_m",
  "Dist_from_EFPC_km",
  "Drainage_area_km2",
  "Developed_lulc"
)

numeric_vars_log <- setdiff(numeric_vars, exclude_vars)

# Log-transform selected columns and add 'log_' prefix
dat <- dat %>%
  mutate(across(
    all_of(numeric_vars_log),
    ~ log10(.),
    .names = "log_{col}"
  ))

# Initialize results data frame for log-transformed variables
normality_results_log_dat <- data.frame(
  Variable  = paste0("log_", numeric_vars_log),
  Normality = NA_character_,
  Skewness  = NA_real_,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Loop over log-transformed columns
for (i in seq_along(numeric_vars_log)) {
  
  var_name <- paste0("log_", numeric_vars_log[i])
  var_data <- dat[[var_name]]
  
  # Ensure numeric
  if (!is.numeric(var_data)) {
    normality_results_log_dat$Normality[i] <- "Not numeric"
    normality_results_log_dat$Skewness[i]  <- NA
    next
  }
  
  # Run Shapiro-Wilk normality test
  test_result <- tryCatch({
    normalTest(var_data, method = "sw")
  }, error = function(e) NULL)
  
  if (!is.null(test_result)) {
    normality_results_log_dat$Normality[i] <-
      ifelse(test_result@test$p.value > 0.05, "Pass", "Fail")
  } else {
    normality_results_log_dat$Normality[i] <- "Error"
  }
  
  # Calculate skewness
  normality_results_log_dat$Skewness[i] <- skewness(var_data)
}

# View results
normality_results_log_dat
```

Save to excel

```{r}
library(openxlsx)

file_path <- "EDA_HA10%_Closed_System.xlsx"

# 1. Load workbook if it exists, otherwise create
if (file.exists(file_path)) {
  wb <- loadWorkbook(file_path)
} else {
  wb <- createWorkbook()
}

# 2. Create sheet if it does NOT exist
sheet_name <- "Normality checks log vars"

if (!sheet_name %in% names(wb)) {
  addWorksheet(wb, sheet_name)
}

# 3. Write data
writeData(wb, sheet_name, normality_results_log_dat)

# 4. Save workbook
saveWorkbook(wb, file_path, overwrite = TRUE)
```

While Normality was still not achieved for most variables, skewness is less pronounced (closer to 0) and small concentration values are better represented on the log-scale.

### iii. Standardized Log-Transformed Variables

Standardize the log-transformed variables and check for normality

```{r}
library(dplyr)

# -----------------------------------------------------
# 1. Standardize all log_ variables + pH
# -----------------------------------------------------
dat <- dat %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      paste0("log_", numeric_vars_log),   # ONLY these log-transformed vars
      ~ as.numeric(scale(.)),
      .names = "{col}_std"
    ),
    pH_std = as.numeric(scale(pH))
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Build vector of standardized variable names
# ------------------------------------------------------
std_vars <- c(
  paste0("log_", numeric_vars_log, "_std"),
  "pH_std"
)

# ------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Initialize results table
# ------------------------------------------------------
normality_results_std_log_dat <- data.frame(
  Variable  = std_vars,
  Normality = NA_character_,
  Skewness  = NA_real_,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# ------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Loop over standardized variables
# ------------------------------------------------------
for (i in seq_along(std_vars)) {

  var_name <- std_vars[i]
  var_data <- dat[[var_name]]

  # Check numeric
  if (!is.numeric(var_data)) {
    normality_results_std_log_dat$Normality[i] <- "Not numeric"
    normality_results_std_log_dat$Skewness[i]  <- NA
    next
  }

  # Shapiro–Wilk test
  test_result <- tryCatch({
    normalTest(var_data, method = "sw")
  }, error = function(e) NULL)

  if (!is.null(test_result)) {
    normality_results_std_log_dat$Normality[i] <-
      ifelse(test_result@test$p.value > 0.05, "Pass", "Fail")
  } else {
    normality_results_std_log_dat$Normality[i] <- "Error"
  }

  # Skewness
  normality_results_std_log_dat$Skewness[i] <- skewness(var_data)
}

# ------------------------------------------------------
# 5. View results
# ------------------------------------------------------
normality_results_std_log_dat
```


## 4. Summary Statistics

We'll calculate summary statistics for all numeric variables across all sites.

```{r}
library(purrr)
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)

# 1. Identify all numeric variables in dat
numeric_vars <- names(dat)[sapply(dat, is.numeric)]

# 2. Mode function (same as you had)
get_mode <- function(x) {
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  if (length(x) == 0) return(NA)
  ux <- unique(x)
  ux[which.max(tabulate(match(x, ux)))]
}

# 3. Compute summary stats for ALL numeric variables
summary_numeric_table <- map_dfr(numeric_vars, function(colname) {
  vec <- dat[[colname]]
  n_non_na <- sum(!is.na(vec))
  tibble(
    variable = colname,
    mean     = mean(vec, na.rm = TRUE),
    median   = median(vec, na.rm = TRUE),
    mode     = get_mode(vec),
    variance = var(vec, na.rm = TRUE),
    se       = sd(vec, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n_non_na)
  )
}) %>%
  arrange(variable)

# 4. View
summary_numeric_table
```

Save to excel

```{r}
library(openxlsx)

file_path <- "EDA_HA10%_Closed_System.xlsx"

# 1. Load workbook if it exists, otherwise create
if (file.exists(file_path)) {
  wb <- loadWorkbook(file_path)
} else {
  wb <- createWorkbook()

# 2. Create sheet if it does NOT exist

if (!sheet_name %in% names(wb)) {
  addWorksheet(wb, sheet_name)

# 3. Write data
```
